title: Create ground where black swans can live
header_line: My analysis of one book on negotiation. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What can you do to uncover an unlikely chance, not wait for it?
A student said that asking open-ended questions is one way to create them, and then listening more consciously.
Another said: not assuming something you do not know, asking questions and using the tactics from the book, paying attention to listening.
I said that you create the fertile ground: if you create the ground where black swans can live and eat and drink and swim, then you see them everywhere.
I said that naturally you attract like-minded people, people on life-long missions with you, with your dreams and motivations.
A student said that black swans are not something you need to wait for; you can take actions to uncover them yourself.
I said that now you can drive down the street and say there is a black swan: we meet people who become little moments in our life that open bigger parts of it.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you will not assume.
Write the ground you could prepare.
Write one action to uncover a chance this week.

check.q: What did a student say creates black swans?
What did I say you create?
What did a student say about waiting?
choices: You do not need to wait

recap: Prepare the ground. Ask open questions. Do not wait.
